predecessors.name: Zhou dynasty
predecessors.text: the valley of Qin, 'modern Qingshui and Zhangjiachuan in Gansu', where King Xiao of Zhou gave Feizi a fief

successors.name: Qin dynasty
successors.text: the unified realm of 221, drawn by Cliopatria as the Qin row to 219 and as the Qin Dynasty row from 218

ledger.x: 897: Feizi receives the fief of Qin from King Xiao of Zhou.
822: King Xuan of Zhou awards Quanqiu to the Qin.
About 821: Duke Zhuang moves the seat from Qinyi to Quanqiu.
776: Duke Xiang holds Qian.
776: the Qin capital moves east from Quanqiu to Qian.
770: King Ping enfeoffs Duke Xiang and promises Qin 'the lands west of Qishan'.
About 750: Qin holds Guanzhong.
413: Wei begins to take Qin's land west of the Yellow River.
409: the fighting for the west bank ends (the page's last year of 413-409).
409: Qin has lost its land west of the Yellow River to Wei.
350: Shang Yang moves the capital to Xianyang.
341: Shang Yang attacks Wei.
328: the fight for the west bank ends in Qin's favour (Zhang Yi's campaign).
328: Zhang Yi's campaign wins the land west of the Yellow River.
325: Huiwen styles himself King of Qin.
316: Qin conquers Shu.
316: Qin conquers Ba, with Shu.
By 315: Qin holds eastern Gansu.
By 315: the remaining land of Cliopatria's 315 shape (221 Shaanxi cells below Guanzhong, the Hubei and Henan margin).
ledger.cp: Rong, Shu and Chu border lands

ledger.x: About 312: Qin seizes Hanzhong from Chu.
301: Qin seizes Chongqiu.
299: Qin captures eight Chu cities.
290: Wei cedes Hedong.
286: Qin takes Anyi, the old Wei capital.
278: Bai Qi captures Ying.
260: Qin wins at Changping and holds Shangdang.
About 260: Qin holds Taiyuan.
256: Qin ends the Zhou royal line.
249: Qin annexes the East Zhou remnant.
230: Qin conquers Han.
229: Qin attacks Zhao.
228: Handan falls and the fighting for Zhao's core ends.
228: Qin takes Handan and Zhao.
226: Qin takes Ji.
225: Wang Ben floods Daliang and Wei surrenders.
224: Qin invades Chu.
223: the war ends with Chu's fall.
223: Wang Jian takes Shouchun and Chu ends.
222: Qin takes Liaodong and ends Yan.
222: Qin takes Dai.
222: Wang Jian and Meng Wu take the Wuyue region.
221: Qi surrenders and China is united.
221: Ying Zheng declares himself Qin Shi Huang, First Emperor of Qin.
219: data handoff to the Qin dynasty.

wars.name: Wei conquest of Qin's western land
wars.outcome: Wei took the land west of the Yellow River from Qin.

wars.name: Qin-Jin war of 645
wars.outcome: Qin won; the page says Jin 'agreed to cede land to end the conflict' and names no place.

wars.name: Battle of Yao
wars.outcome: Jin ambushed the Qin army returning from a planned attack on Zheng; no territory changed.

wars.name: Qin-Wei wars over the west bank (Shang Yang and Zhang Yi)
wars.outcome: Wei ceded the land west of the Yellow River to Qin; Zhang Yi's 328 campaign 'acquired a large part of Wei'.

wars.name: Qin's conquest of Shu and Ba
wars.outcome: Qin annexed Shu and Ba; the marquisates of Shu (Prince Tong 313-311, Prince Yun 308-301) were fiefs of Qin princes.

wars.name: Battles of Danyang and Lantian
wars.outcome: Qin defeated Chu and seized Hanzhong; Shaoling fell in 311.

wars.name: Qin attacks on Chu, 302-299
wars.outcome: Qin seized Chongqiu (301) and eight Chu cities (299) and held King Huai hostage at Wuguan.

wars.name: Battle of Yique and the Hedong cessions
wars.outcome: Bai Qi 'defeated the two major states at Yique' (293); Wei conceded 400 li of Hedong (290); Qin took Anyi (286).

wars.name: Qin's capture of Ying
wars.outcome: Bai Qi captured Ying and Qin set up the Nan Commandery.

wars.name: Battle of Changping
wars.outcome: Qin cut off Shangdang from Han (262), Han's commanders gave it to Zhao, and Qin 'defeated a 450,000-strong Zhao army at Changping in 260 BC'.

wars.name: Qin conquest of the Zhou
wars.outcome: Qin took Wangcheng in 256 and the East Zhou remnant in 249.

wars.name: Qin's wars of unification
wars.outcome: Qin conquered the six states in order: Han 230, Zhao 228, Yan 226 and 222, Wei 225, Chu 223, Qi 221, and the First Emperor took his title in 221.

certainty.note: Qin's lands and the Yellow River line are known from a few sentences; the western fiefs (Qinyi, Quanqiu, Qian) are circles round named counties.
The Sichuan edge (Shu, Ba) and the Chu frontier (Wuguan, Hanzhong, Nan Commandery) are approximate; the Hedong and Shangdang frontiers follow the cessions.
The unification borders are commandery outlines the pages do not draw; the Liaodong and Wuyue edges are the softest.
